subject: physics
question_text: Distinguish between free oscillations, damped oscillations and forced oscillations, with one example each.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Free oscillations
lines: Free oscillations: a body displaced once and
then left alone oscillates at its OWN natural
frequency, with an amplitude that does not
change. Example: a tuning fork struck once in
steps.why: Free oscillation is an idealisation — a real body always loses some energy, so the constant amplitude is a limiting case.
common_mistakes: Giving a real swinging pendulum as the example; that is damped, because air resistance acts on it.

recall.must_convey: That free oscillations happen at the natural frequency with unchanging amplitude, once the body is left alone.

steps.label: Damped oscillations
lines: Damped oscillations: friction or air resistance
takes energy away from the body, so the
amplitude decreases steadily with time while
the frequency stays nearly the same. The fall
Example: a simple pendulum swinging in air.
steps.why: The energy is not lost, only moved: it leaves the oscillation as heat in the surrounding air.
common_mistakes: Saying the frequency falls quickly as well; for light damping it barely changes.

recall.must_convey: That damping removes energy so the amplitude decreases with time while the frequency is nearly unchanged.

steps.label: Forced oscillations
lines: Forced oscillations: an outside periodic force
keeps the body oscillating at the FORCED
Example: a bridge shaken by feet marching
steps.why: In a forced oscillation the body oscillates at the driving frequency, not at its own — which is why the special case where the two are equal builds such a large amplitude.
common_mistakes: Saying a forced oscillation always happens at the natural frequency; that is only the resonance case.

recall.must_convey: That in forced oscillations an outside periodic force drives the body at the forced frequency, and resonance is when the two frequencies agree.
